newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi repeats claim in row with China, urges talks.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi repeats claim in row with China, urges talks.

text.p: Vietnam on Thursday reiterated its claim to sovereignty over an offshore area where China is exploring for gas and called for negotiations to resolve the dispute.

"As we have clearly stated, the area where the Kan Tan III rig is operating completely lies within Vietnam's exclusive economic zone and on the continental shelf," a Foreign Ministry spokesman told a news conference. "At the same time we always advocate resolving disputes through diplomatic channels."

"Vietnam advocates solving all disputes through negotiations. Parties concerned should exercise self-restraint, doing nothing to further complicate the situation or resort to the use of force or threats," the spokesman said.

He said it was Vietnam's wish that, for the sake of friendship between the two countries and peace and cooperation in the region, its legitimate demand would have a positive response and draw support from regional and world public opinion.

Vietnam said last weekend it had protested to China, demanding immediate withdrawal of the rig and accompanying vessels from an area 64.5 nautical miles off its central coastline. Beijing responded that the drilling rig was in Chinese waters and that its activities were above reproach.
The two nations have competing claims on areas along their land border, on parts of the Tonkin Gulf and on the Paracel Island chain. They are also among six regional claimants to the Spratly Islands.
